title: दानबहादुरको रिटमाथि अर्को पेशी मंसिर ९ लाई तोकियो, प्रहरी हेडक्वार्टरका अधिवक्तामार्फत म्याद तामेल गर्न आदेश
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । सर्वोच्च अदालतले नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक डा. मनोजकुमार केसीको नाममा जारी भएको म्याद प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयका कानुन व्यवसायी (अधिवक्ता) मार्फत तामेल गर्न आदेश दिएको छ । अदालतका तामेलदार म्याद बुझाउन जाँदा प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयले बुझ्न इन्कार गरेपछि सोमबार संयुक्त इजलासले यस्तो आदेश दिएको हो। न्यायाधीशद्वय हरिप्रसाद फुयाल र नित्यानन्द पाण्डेयको संयुक्त इजलासले निवर्तमान आईजीपी दानबहादुर कार्कीले दायर गरेको उत्प्रेषण रिटमाथि सुनुवाइ गर्दै उक्त आदेश जारी गरेको हो। के भएको थियो म्याद तामेलीमा ? सर्वोच्च अदालतले गत मंसिर ४ गते आईजीपी डा. केसीका नाममा म्याद जारी गरेको थियो । अदालतको आदेशमा उल्लेख भएअनुसार उक्त म्याद बुझाउन अदालतका तामेलदार प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालय पुग्दा कार्यालयका कर्मचारीले ‘सम्बन्धित व्यक्ति (आईजीपी) मिटिङमा जानुभएको छ, फर्केर आउनुहुन्छ’ भनी कार्यालय समयसम्म पर्खाएका थिए। तर, कार्यालय समय सकिँदासम्म पनि आईजीपी केसी उपस्थित नभएको र कार्यालयले समेत म्याद बुझ्न इन्कार गरेपछि तामेलदारले म्याद तामेल हुन नसकेको प्रतिवेदन अदालतमा पेस गरेका थिए। सोमबारको सुनुवाइका क्रममा विपक्षी प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयका तर्फबाट उपस्थित अधिवक्ताले उक्त म्याद ’प्राविधिक कारणले बुझ्न नसकिएको’ भन्दै पुनः म्याद जारी भए फिर्ता नहुने प्रतिबद्धतासहित इजलाससमक्ष अनुरोध गरेका थिए। सोही अनुरोधबमोजिम इजलासले प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयलाई प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने अधिवक्तामार्फत नै मंसिर ४ गतेको म्याद बुझाई नियमानुसार पेस गर्न आदेश दिएको हो। इजलासले पेसीमा प्राथमिकता दिई पालो समेत आउने गरी आगामी मंसिर ९ गते बुधबार लागि अर्को पेसी तोक्न र सोको जानकारी महान्यायाधिवक्ताको कार्यालय समेतलाई दिन आदेश दिएको छ। सरकारले गत कात्तिक १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकमार्फत दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकको जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाएर प्रधानमन्त्रीको विशेष सुरक्षा सल्लाहकारमा सरुवा गर्दै एआईजी डा. मनोजकुमार केसीलाई आईजीपीमा बढुवा गरेको थियो। सरकारले गैरकानुनी रूपमा आफूलाई पदमुक्त गरेको दाबी गर्दै कार्कीले उक्त निर्णय बदर गरी आईजीपीमा पुनर्बहालीको मागसहित कात्तिक २० गते सर्वोच्च अदालतमा रिट दायर गरेका थिए । यसअघि मंसिर २ गते न्यायाधीश श्रीकान्त पौडेलको एकल इजलासले अल्पकालीन अन्तरिम आदेश नदिई दुवै पक्षलाई छलफलका लागि सोमबार (मंसिर ७) बोलाएको थियो। Kathmandu. The Supreme Court has ordered that the summons issued in the name of Inspector General of Nepal Police Dr. Manoj Kumar KC be served through the legal practitioner (advocate) of the Police Headquarters. The joint bench issued the order on Monday after the Police Headquarters refused to accept the summons when the court's clerk went to serve it. A joint bench of Justices Hari Prasad Phuyal and Nityanand Pandey issued the order while hearing a writ petition filed by outgoing IGP Dan Bahadur Karki. What happened in the deadline? The Supreme Court had issued a summons in the name of IGP Dr. KC on November 20. As mentioned in the court order, when the court's clerk reached the police headquarters to submit the summons, the office staff had waited until office hours, saying, "The person concerned (IGP) has gone to a meeting and will return." However, IGP KC was not present even after the office hours ended and the office also refused to accept the summons, so the court clerk submitted a report to the court stating that the summons could not be served. During Monday's hearing, the lawyer representing the opposing Police Headquarters had requested the bench, stating that the deadline was 'unintelligible due to technical reasons' and promising not to withdraw it if it was reissued. In accordance with the same request, the bench ordered the Police Headquarters to submit the deadline dated 19th November through the lawyer representing the same. The bench has ordered to schedule another hearing for Wednesday, November 21, giving priority to the case and also to inform the Attorney General's Office. The government had removed Dan Bahadur Karki from the post of Inspector General of Police through a cabinet meeting on November 18 and transferred him to the post of Special Security Advisor to the Prime Minister, and promoted AIG Dr. Manoj Kumar KC to IGP. Claiming that the government had illegally removed him from the post, Karki had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on November 20, seeking his reinstatement as IGP and quashing the decision. Earlier, on Mangsir 2, a single bench of Justice Shrikant Poudel had summoned both sides for discussions on Monday (Mangsir 7) without issuing a short-term interim order.

सर्वोच्च अदालतले गत मंसिर ४ गते आईजीपी डा. केसीका नाममा म्याद जारी गरेको थियो । अदालतको आदेशमा उल्लेख भएअनुसार उक्त म्याद बुझाउन अदालतका तामेलदार प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालय पुग्दा कार्यालयका कर्मचारीले ‘सम्बन्धित व्यक्ति (आईजीपी) मिटिङमा जानुभएको छ, फर्केर आउनुहुन्छ’ भनी कार्यालय समयसम्म पर्खाएका थिए। तर, कार्यालय समय सकिँदासम्म पनि आईजीपी केसी उपस्थित नभएको र कार्यालयले समेत म्याद बुझ्न इन्कार गरेपछि तामेलदारले म्याद तामेल हुन नसकेको प्रतिवेदन अदालतमा पेस गरेका थिए। सोमबारको सुनुवाइका क्रममा विपक्षी प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयका तर्फबाट उपस्थित अधिवक्ताले उक्त म्याद ’प्राविधिक कारणले बुझ्न नसकिएको’ भन्दै पुनः म्याद जारी भए फिर्ता नहुने प्रतिबद्धतासहित इजलाससमक्ष अनुरोध गरेका थिए। सोही अनुरोधबमोजिम इजलासले प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयलाई प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने अधिवक्तामार्फत नै मंसिर ४ गतेको म्याद बुझाई नियमानुसार पेस गर्न आदेश दिएको हो। इजलासले पेसीमा प्राथमिकता दिई पालो समेत आउने गरी आगामी मंसिर ९ गते बुधबार लागि अर्को पेसी तोक्न र सोको जानकारी महान्यायाधिवक्ताको कार्यालय समेतलाई दिन आदेश दिएको छ। सरकारले गत कात्तिक १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकमार्फत दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकको जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाएर प्रधानमन्त्रीको विशेष सुरक्षा सल्लाहकारमा सरुवा गर्दै एआईजी डा. मनोजकुमार केसीलाई आईजीपीमा बढुवा गरेको थियो। सरकारले गैरकानुनी रूपमा आफूलाई पदमुक्त गरेको दाबी गर्दै कार्कीले उक्त निर्णय बदर गरी आईजीपीमा पुनर्बहालीको मागसहित कात्तिक २० गते सर्वोच्च अदालतमा रिट दायर गरेका थिए । यसअघि मंसिर २ गते न्यायाधीश श्रीकान्त पौडेलको एकल इजलासले अल्पकालीन अन्तरिम आदेश नदिई दुवै पक्षलाई छलफलका लागि सोमबार (मंसिर ७) बोलाएको थियो। Kathmandu. The Supreme Court has ordered that the summons issued in the name of Inspector General of Nepal Police Dr. Manoj Kumar KC be served through the legal practitioner (advocate) of the Police Headquarters. The joint bench issued the order on Monday after the Police Headquarters refused to accept the summons when the court's clerk went to serve it. A joint bench of Justices Hari Prasad Phuyal and Nityanand Pandey issued the order while hearing a writ petition filed by outgoing IGP Dan Bahadur Karki. What happened in the deadline? The Supreme Court had issued a summons in the name of IGP Dr. KC on November 20. As mentioned in the court order, when the court's clerk reached the police headquarters to submit the summons, the office staff had waited until office hours, saying, "The person concerned (IGP) has gone to a meeting and will return." However, IGP KC was not present even after the office hours ended and the office also refused to accept the summons, so the court clerk submitted a report to the court stating that the summons could not be served. During Monday's hearing, the lawyer representing the opposing Police Headquarters had requested the bench, stating that the deadline was 'unintelligible due to technical reasons' and promising not to withdraw it if it was reissued. In accordance with the same request, the bench ordered the Police Headquarters to submit the deadline dated 19th November through the lawyer representing the same. The bench has ordered to schedule another hearing for Wednesday, November 21, giving priority to the case and also to inform the Attorney General's Office. The government had removed Dan Bahadur Karki from the post of Inspector General of Police through a cabinet meeting on November 18 and transferred him to the post of Special Security Advisor to the Prime Minister, and promoted AIG Dr. Manoj Kumar KC to IGP. Claiming that the government had illegally removed him from the post, Karki had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on November 20, seeking his reinstatement as IGP and quashing the decision. Earlier, on Mangsir 2, a single bench of Justice Shrikant Poudel had summoned both sides for discussions on Monday (Mangsir 7) without issuing a short-term interim order.

सर्वोच्च अदालतले गत मंसिर ४ गते आईजीपी डा. केसीका नाममा म्याद जारी गरेको थियो । अदालतको आदेशमा उल्लेख भएअनुसार उक्त म्याद बुझाउन अदालतका तामेलदार प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालय पुग्दा कार्यालयका कर्मचारीले ‘सम्बन्धित व्यक्ति (आईजीपी) मिटिङमा जानुभएको छ, फर्केर आउनुहुन्छ’ भनी कार्यालय समयसम्म पर्खाएका थिए।

तर, कार्यालय समय सकिँदासम्म पनि आईजीपी केसी उपस्थित नभएको र कार्यालयले समेत म्याद बुझ्न इन्कार गरेपछि तामेलदारले म्याद तामेल हुन नसकेको प्रतिवेदन अदालतमा पेस गरेका थिए।

सोमबारको सुनुवाइका क्रममा विपक्षी प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयका तर्फबाट उपस्थित अधिवक्ताले उक्त म्याद ’प्राविधिक कारणले बुझ्न नसकिएको’ भन्दै पुनः म्याद जारी भए फिर्ता नहुने प्रतिबद्धतासहित इजलाससमक्ष अनुरोध गरेका थिए। सोही अनुरोधबमोजिम इजलासले प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयलाई प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने अधिवक्तामार्फत नै मंसिर ४ गतेको म्याद बुझाई नियमानुसार पेस गर्न आदेश दिएको हो।

इजलासले पेसीमा प्राथमिकता दिई पालो समेत आउने गरी आगामी मंसिर ९ गते बुधबार लागि अर्को पेसी तोक्न र सोको जानकारी महान्यायाधिवक्ताको कार्यालय समेतलाई दिन आदेश दिएको छ।

सरकारले गत कात्तिक १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकमार्फत दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकको जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाएर प्रधानमन्त्रीको विशेष सुरक्षा सल्लाहकारमा सरुवा गर्दै एआईजी डा. मनोजकुमार केसीलाई आईजीपीमा बढुवा गरेको थियो। सरकारले गैरकानुनी रूपमा आफूलाई पदमुक्त गरेको दाबी गर्दै कार्कीले उक्त निर्णय बदर गरी आईजीपीमा पुनर्बहालीको मागसहित कात्तिक २० गते सर्वोच्च अदालतमा रिट दायर गरेका थिए ।

यसअघि मंसिर २ गते न्यायाधीश श्रीकान्त पौडेलको एकल इजलासले अल्पकालीन अन्तरिम आदेश नदिई दुवै पक्षलाई छलफलका लागि सोमबार (मंसिर ७) बोलाएको थियो।

Kathmandu. The Supreme Court has ordered that the summons issued in the name of Inspector General of Nepal Police Dr. Manoj Kumar KC be served through the legal practitioner (advocate) of the Police Headquarters. The joint bench issued the order on Monday after the Police Headquarters refused to accept the summons when the court's clerk went to serve it. A joint bench of Justices Hari Prasad Phuyal and Nityanand Pandey issued the order while hearing a writ petition filed by outgoing IGP Dan Bahadur Karki. What happened in the deadline? The Supreme Court had issued a summons in the name of IGP Dr. KC on November 20. As mentioned in the court order, when the court's clerk reached the police headquarters to submit the summons, the office staff had waited until office hours, saying, "The person concerned (IGP) has gone to a meeting and will return." However, IGP KC was not present even after the office hours ended and the office also refused to accept the summons, so the court clerk submitted a report to the court stating that the summons could not be served. During Monday's hearing, the lawyer representing the opposing Police Headquarters had requested the bench, stating that the deadline was 'unintelligible due to technical reasons' and promising not to withdraw it if it was reissued. In accordance with the same request, the bench ordered the Police Headquarters to submit the deadline dated 19th November through the lawyer representing the same. The bench has ordered to schedule another hearing for Wednesday, November 21, giving priority to the case and also to inform the Attorney General's Office. The government had removed Dan Bahadur Karki from the post of Inspector General of Police through a cabinet meeting on November 18 and transferred him to the post of Special Security Advisor to the Prime Minister, and promoted AIG Dr. Manoj Kumar KC to IGP. Claiming that the government had illegally removed him from the post, Karki had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on November 20, seeking his reinstatement as IGP and quashing the decision. Earlier, on Mangsir 2, a single bench of Justice Shrikant Poudel had summoned both sides for discussions on Monday (Mangsir 7) without issuing a short-term interim order.
